label: offload30-vs-none-cs4
status_note: All four blocks complete. Blocks A2/B2 were taken under HEAVY AMBIENT LOAD (five subagents: ~25% total CPU, 22 python / 12 node / 9 claude processes, plus Windows Search indexing). That load is recorded rather than hidden because it turned out to be a result, not only a mistake -- see findings.load_sensitivity.
question: Does MoE expert offload have to be enabled, and what does it cost?

session_clock.note: #1490: measurements start from a rebooted machine. A deliberate reboot at 14:58 applied a registry change; every block here is from that boot.

resource_envelope.envelope_note: #1485: a version stamp is not a machine. The pinning limit and both memory figures are recorded because a June config that fitted stopped fitting and the quantity that moved was one nobody was recording.

config_common.held_constant_note: the micro-GEMM flag is held at 0 on both sides; its own A/B is #1500 and is NOT measured here

method.request: the real captured coder request, 14,094-14,116 prompt tokens, 9 tools
method.nonce: EVERY measured request carries a unique nonce at the HEAD of the first message
method.why_the_nonce: LOAD-BEARING. A first version of this harness reused one prompt, so --enable_prefix_caching served every measured run: it read 285.404 s for the first request and 0.485 s / 0.765 s for the two behind it. Without the nonce this measures the cache and reports it as prefill.
method.streaming: yes -- TTFT is separable from generation

findings.memory_returned_derivation: mean no-offload adapter peak (19.754) minus mean offload adapter peak (15.535)
findings.no_offload_EXCEEDS_the_aperture: peaks 19.697 and 19.811 GiB against an 18.000 GiB aperture and a 16.342 GiB reported ceiling. It does not fail outright, but it is over budget -- exactly as the 2026-08-31 measurement recorded.
findings.free_ram_floor: no-offload drove available system RAM to 0.74 GiB in B2 and 3.20 GiB in B1. With offload: 3.60 and 7.29 GiB. 0.74 GiB free is the territory where the machine stops being usable for anything else, which is the operator's stated reason for wanting offload.
findings.load_sensitivity: THE OFFLOAD PATH IS LOAD-SENSITIVE AND THE NO-OFFLOAD PATH IS NOT. Offload first-turn TTFT: 200.6/220.8/238.6 s quiet, 588.9 s loaded. No-offload: 44.8/47.0/64.3 s quiet, 52.5 s loaded. Mechanism: offload streams 30% of the MoE experts from SYSTEM RAM on every token, so on an integrated GPU sharing one LPDDR5X pool it competes with all other memory traffic. Offload's cost is therefore ~3.4x on an idle machine and ~11x on a busy one, NOT a fixed multiplier.
findings.operational_consequence: 588.9 s sits just under the 600 s ACP idle bound that kills a candidate. On a quiet box offload has large headroom; under load it has almost none. The 23:00 run must be quiet for this configuration to be safe, and nothing currently enforces that.
findings.offload_is_CHEAPER_to_load: 12.05/15.06 s with offload against 42.18/57.07 s without
findings.the_first_turn_is_paid_once: turn 2 of the same conversation: 1.322/2.484 s with offload, 1.708/0.829 s without. The 12,461-token floor is cached after turn 1.
findings.prefix_cache_magnitude: novel prefix 285.404 s to first token; identical prefix 0.485 s and 0.765 s.
findings.NO_DECODE_DIFFERENCE_ESTABLISHED: offload 14.57/18.67/9.18/12.97 tok/s; no-offload 6.13/6.44/11.89/11.94. The ranges OVERLAP. An earlier claim of a 2.4x decode advantage for offload rested on one block against one block and is RETRACTED. Every figure came from a generation truncated at 67-221 tokens by a tool call, so none is a sustained rate and none should be quoted as one.

operator_decision_2026_09_01.rationale: the memory it frees is worth a one-time per-conversation prefill cost, PROVIDED sustained decode and long-prompt quality hold
conditions_not_yet_evidenced: sustained decode -- every decode figure taken today came from a generation that stopped at 67-218 tokens on a tool call, which is a burst dominated by ramp-up and MUST NOT be quoted as a sustained rate
long-prompt answer quality under offload -- no instrument exists for this; the evals/ suites target the assistant's 14B, not the coder

not_measured: SUSTAINED decode -- every decode figure here came from a truncated generation. A corrected instrument keeping the full prompt floor and forbidding the tool call is being built; until it runs, this project has NO honest sustained-decode figure for the coder at a realistic prefill.
answer quality or long-prompt degradation under offload -- no instrument exists; the evals/ suites target the assistant's 14B, not the coder
whether the 57 -> 87 pinning-limit change contributed anything: it moved the reported ceiling by 0 bytes and no 57% control was run after the reboot, so its effect on real allocation is UNKNOWN
offload ratios other than 30, cache sizes other than 4, concurrency
a controlled quiet-vs-loaded pair -- the load in A2/B2 was accidental, not designed, so the load-sensitivity finding rests on 2 loaded blocks against 4 quiet ones and deserves a deliberate repeat

retraction.what_was_claimed: An earlier version of this file and of the PERFORMANCE_LOG entry stated 'offload is NOT required to fit', citing no-offload committing 15.576 GiB against a 16.342 GiB ceiling, and called start-llm.ps1's comment a false assertion.
retraction.why_it_was_wrong: 15.576 GiB was a LOAD-TIME sample, not a peak. Continuous sampling across the whole block gives no-offload peaks of 19.697 and 19.811 GiB -- ABOVE the 18.000 GiB driver aperture. The launcher's comment, which cited cache_size 2 without offload measuring 18.04 and 18.18 GiB over budget, is CORROBORATED.
retraction.the_irony_kept_deliberately: This same file already warned that a load-time sample is not a peak. The warning was written and then violated in the same document.
retraction.status: start-llm.ps1's offload comment stands. No correction to it is warranted.

superseded_note: All four blocks completed, but at 15:45 on the same day the GPU ceiling was RESTORED to 27,031,388,160 B (25.175 GiB). Every figure here was measured against a 16.342 GiB horizon that no longer exists. The measurements are valid; the machine state they describe is gone. The cause was TWO registry keys that had disagreed for a week: GraphicsDrivers\MemoryManager\SystemPartitionCommitLimitPercentage governs the REAL DXGK budget, and Class\{4d36e968-...}�1\GMM\GpuSystemMemoryPinninglimit governs what OpenVINO REPORTS. The real budget fell to 57% on 2026-08-26 -- that was the regression -- while the reported figure still read 25 GiB, so every investigation between then and now was reading an instrument that was lying. Verified: alignDown(floor(0.94*(P/100*33630777344))-450MiB,4096) gives 17,547,509,760 at P=57 and 27,031,388,160 at P=87, matching both historical readings to the byte.
what_survives_the_supersession: offload returns 4.22 GiB of shared GPU memory (peaks 15.535 vs 19.754 mean) -- a config-vs-config delta, not a ceiling-relative one, so it is unaffected
the free-RAM floor: 0.74 GiB without offload against 3.60-7.29 GiB with it
the load-sensitivity asymmetry: offload 200.6/220.8/238.6 s quiet vs 588.9 s loaded; no-offload 44.8/47.0/64.3 s quiet vs 52.5 s loaded. A mechanism, not a ceiling artefact.
the first turn is paid once: turn 2 costs 0.83-2.48 s in every block
offload loads the server 3x faster: 12-15 s vs 42-57 s
no decode difference is established, and the figures are all from truncated generations
what_does_NOT_survive: the claim that no-offload 'EXCEEDS the aperture' at 19.7/19.8 GiB peaks. That was measured against an 18.000 GiB aperture which was itself downstream of the wrong pinning limit. Against the restored 27.25 GiB budget, 19.8 GiB is comfortably inside it -- and no-offload did in fact run fine and fast (52.5-64.3 s) throughout.

the ca9b4a36 retraction's conclusion that start-llm.ps1's over-budget comment is 'corroborated'. That comment was written when the real budget WAS 17.85 GiB and was correct then; whether it is correct now is an open question, not a settled one.
any absolute headroom claim -- all of them were computed against 16.342 GiB
